subject: Request: Onward-transfer permission for LogStream analytics processor (EU SCCs / HIPAA?)
messages:
From: Sarah Chen <sarah@pulsemx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: New analytics processor (LogStream) onboarding + onward-transfer permission request

Hi Ben,

Hope you’re well — quick notice from PulseMetrics. We recently selected LogStream (logstream.ai) as our new log analytics/processing subprocessor for a subset of audit and feature-usage logs that PulseMetrics forwards to partners. Were in the bookkeeping phase and need Redwood sign-off for onward-transfer of any Redwood-derived logs that are placed into our pipeline (the usual limited set: request IDs, timestamps, anonymized route and error tags).

Attached: vendor_roster_v4.pdf (current PulseMetrics roster), logstream_scc_summary.pdf (LogStream answers and SCC mapping). Also attaching our proposed DPA redline for Redwood to review (dpa_redline.docx).

Two quick questions wed like cleared before we finalize the rollout:
- Does Redwood require a specific SCC execution flow for this kind of processor-to-processor transfer, or will the existing DPA + Standard Contractual Clauses between Redwood and PulseMetrics suffice?
- Any HIPAA considerations if a small portion of logs come from a healthcare customer (we'll mark/segregate those records, but want to be sure).

If you can confirm permission to onboard LogStream (subject to your legal/security checks) and list any required evidence/doc we should send (SOC/SIG/etc.), that would be great. Were aiming for the integration to go live the week of Dec 14.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min sync if helpful.

Best,
Sarah Chen
Head of Partnerships, PulseMetrics
attachments: vendor_roster_v4.pdf, logstream_scc_summary.pdf, dpa_redline.docx

---
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@pulsemx.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: New analytics processor (LogStream) onboarding + onward-transfer permission request

Thanks Sarah — looping in Legal and Security for quick review.

Lauren / Evelyn — FYI PulseMetrics intends to onboard LogStream (a third-party processor) to handle parsed audit logs derived from Redwood-integrated flows. Theyve attached a SCC mapping doc and a vendor roster. Immediate asks:
1) Legal: confirm whether our standing DPA + executed SCCs with PulseMetrics cover onward transfers to LogStream (or if we need direct SCC addendum or execution between Redwood and LogStream).
2) Security: please flag anything from the SCC summary or roster that looks like a redline (cross-border storage, subprocessors with shared-cloud tenancy, HIPAA posture).

Sarah — can you also confirm: will LogStream have persistent access to raw message content, or only metadata and anonymized identifiers? In our case we need to limit raw PII exposure (if any).

Ben
VP, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

---
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sarah Chen <sarah@pulsemx.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: New analytics processor (LogStream) onboarding + onward-transfer permission request

Hi Sarah / Ben,

Thanks for the note and attachments — reviewed the roster and LogStream SCC mapping at a high level. A few items and requested evidence before we can provide formal permission:

1) SCCs: Redwood requires either (A) an SCC execution path that binds LogStream directly (preferred), or (B) a Flow-down clause in PulseMetrics DPA that provides the same level of protection and audit rights. The SCC summary attached looks like a mapping, but we need the executed SCC agreement or confirmation that PulseMetrics will accept liability for onward transfers on Redwood's behalf.

2) SOC/SIG evidence: please provide LogStream's most recent SOC2 Type II summary (top-line report or SOC summary letter) or an up-to-date SIG Lite questionnaire. The SOC2 summary can be redacted for client names; we just need control coverage and period.

3) Data residency and encryption: clarify whether LogStream will store any material in non-EU regions. If so, list regions and describe at-rest encryption and key management.

4) HIPAA: if the logs could include PHI elements for a healthcare customer, we will need either (i) a Business Associate Agreement flowed through PulseMetrics with LogStream, or (ii) evidence LogStream is willing/able to sign Standard BAA terms. Can PulseMetrics confirm whether the health-customer logs will be routed via a different retention policy?

5) Access controls/audit: requested: a scoped access matrix for LogStream engineers (SRE vs. engineering vs. ops), and whether they use multi-tenant clusters or dedicated tenancy for customers with regulated data.

To speed this up, Ive attached a short checklist (we use internally) that covers the items above; if you can populate and return it we can give provisional permission while Security completes the review.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
attachments: onboarding_checklist_redwood.docx

---
From: Sarah Chen <sarah@pulsemx.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Andre M. <andre@logstream.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: New analytics processor (LogStream) onboarding + onward-transfer permission request

Hi Lauren / Ben — appreciate the quick turn. Answers below and attaching the SOC2 summary and a CSV export of the current roster.

Quick answers:
- LogStream will only receive pseudonymized IDs, timestamps, route/error tags, and aggregated counters. No raw message bodies or PII.
- LogStream is willing to sign SCCs that flow from Redwood or execute an SCC addendum directly. They have an EU data center footprint but can be contractually restricted to EU-only storage for this integration.
- SOC2: attaching soc2_summary.pdf (summary letter, period Apr 2025 - Mar 2026).
- HIPAA: PulseMetrics will not route any PHI to LogStream for the initial roll-out. For the small healthcare customer, logs will be redirected to a segregated retention bucket managed by PulseMetrics; we will only forward non-PHI metadata to LogStream. If the customer later requests PHI-derived analytics, PulseMetrics will coordinate BAA flow-down and ask LogStream to sign.
- Access controls: LogStream uses multi-tenant clusters but offers dedicated tenancy and VPC isolation for regulated customers; Andre is copied to confirm.

Attachments: soc2_summary.pdf, vendor_roster_v4.csv

Action requested: can Redwood provide provisional permission to proceed with onboarding (subject to execution of SCC or written flow-down confirmation)? Wed like to move to engineering kickoff next week.

Regards,
Sarah Chen
Head of Partnerships, PulseMetrics
